rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should test a configuration that isolates key design choices. This experiment tests the combination of scgpt (advanced RNA encoder), resnet50 (standard image encoder), transformer aggregation (complex interaction modeling), and concat fusion (simple modality combination). It clarifies whether advanced encoders and complex aggregation methods improve performance, which are critical decisions with high uncertainty. This is the best use of the first experiment as it provides a baseline for comparing other configurations and informs future exploration of more complex interactions.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, resnet50, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves 0.470968 accuracy. This experiment tests changing fusion from concat to weighted, isolating its impact while keeping other components constant. This clarifies whether weighted fusion improves performance, a critical design choice for multimodal models. It balances exploration of fusion methods with minimal change, avoiding unnecessary complexity.

Existing evidence shows that weighted fusion (config_011) outperforms concat (config_001). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with ViT (while retaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion) improves performance, isolating the effect of the image encoder choice. It builds on the promising direction of weighted fusion and explores a key design decision (image encoder) that could significantly impact results.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder (config_036) outperforms resnet50. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from scgpt to scvi_n200 (a simpler model) while keeping the high-performing image encoder and fusion/aggregation settings (transformer + weighted) could further improve accuracy. This isolates the RNA encoder's impact on performance, a critical design choice with sparse prior evidence.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (vs. avgpool) and concat fusion (vs. weighted) could further improve performance, isolating the impact of these design choices. It builds on the strong foundation of config_039 while exploring critical components of the model architecture.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_039) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing transformer aggregation with avgpool aggregation (while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method consistent) impacts performance, isolating the effect of aggregation. This is critical for understanding if transformer's superiority is robust or if avgpool could offer better results with these encoders.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder and weighted fusion yield high performance (config_039: 0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l (used in config_039) with resnet50 affects performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice. It balances exploitation (building on successful components) and exploration (testing a critical design decision with potential to improve or confirm current trends).

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_039) achieves high accuracy. Testing config_018 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) isolates the effect of the image encoder (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) and fusion method (concat vs weighted). This comparison clarifies whether the image encoder or fusion method is more impactful, leveraging the strong performance of scvi_n200 RNA while varying key components.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and transformer aggregation achieves high performance. This experiment tests whether switching to pca_n2000 RNA encoder and avgpool aggregation (while keeping imagenet_vit_l image encoder and weighted fusion) could improve accuracy. It isolates the impact of RNA encoder and aggregation methods, which are critical design choices with uncertain trade-offs.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieves high accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with pca_n2000 (while keeping other parameters the same) affects performance, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder choice. This is critical for understanding which representation (scvi_n200 vs pca_n2000) drives performance, balancing exploitation of the current high-performing setup with exploration of alternative representations.
